The Visigothic page: 'By 476, he had extended his rule to the Rhone and the Loire' and Arles and Marseille 'occupied under Euric', with no year for the cities (page silent). Arles was taken in 471 and handed back in 475 ('in exchange for the return of Provence', Euric page), so 476 is the retaking that follows Nepos's fall (confidence 1); Provence lies east of the Rhone and has no owner in Cliopatria in 476.
476: the Western court is at Salona. Infobox 'Salona/Spalatum: 475-480'; Nepos 'In Dalmatia: 28 August 475 - 9 May 480'. The shape and the dot move to Dalmatia the year Ravenna falls.

region.text: Italy and the Danube remnant: 'On 4 September 476, Odoacer, leader of the Germanic foederati in Italy, captured Ravenna'

ledger.note: 4 September 476: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus and rules Italy. 'compelling the young emperor Romulus to abdicate on 4 September'; the troops proclaimed him king (rex) on 23 August 476. The Western Roman Empire page's infobox ends the empire here. Nepos keeps Dalmatia in the Eastern Empire's eyes; Odoacer 'only nominally accepted Nepos's rule'.

region.text: Dalmatia, where Nepos was 'murdered on 9 May 480, at his villa near Salona'

ledger.note: 9 May 480: Julius Nepos is murdered and the Western Roman Empire ends. 'Nepos was murdered on 9 May 480, at his villa near Salona'; 'Only in late 481 or 482 did Odoacer invade Dalmatia' (Nepos page), so Dalmatia is Odoacer's from 481/482; the Western Roman Empire page keeps 476 as its end date, with 480 'sometimes used'.

wars.name: Alaric's invasion of Italy

zones.text: Lombardy and Venetia, where the Visigoths campaigned

wars.outcome: The court moved to Ravenna; no land was ceded in the pages read.
wars.note: The page dates the capital move to 401 and the Visigoths' entry into Italy to 402 ('Stilicho was campaigning in Raetia when the Visigoths entered Italy in 402'). Alaric's sack of Rome, 24 August 410 (Constantine III page), moved no border.

wars.name: Crossing of the Rhine
wars.outcome: The tribes ravaged Gaul and 'in autumn 409 much of the barbarian force entered Hispania'; the Rhine line was not restored until Constantius and the Burgundian settlement (413).
wars.note: Begins 31 December 406 ('several tribes of barbarian invaders, including the Vandals'); the Fall page gives 'the Crossing of the Rhine in 406 (or 405)'.

wars.name: Revolt of Constantine III
wars.outcome: Constantine took Britain (407), Gaul and, through his son Constans, Hispania (408), was recognised as co-emperor by Honorius in early 409, lost Hispania to Gerontius and Maximus in 409, was reduced to Arles by Gerontius in 411, and was beheaded in August or September 411 after Constantius's arrival; Gaul returned to Honorius, Britain and Hispania did not.
wars.note: Recognition 'In early 409'; the Britain page has the Britons expel his magistrates 'in 409 or 410' and Honorius write 'a rescript to British communities in 410'.

wars.name: Visigothic settlement in southern Gaul
wars.outcome: The Visigoths took Narbonne and Toulouse (413) and were settled in southwestern Gaul under Wallia in 418, 'as a vassal federation' with Toulouse as capital; the status lasted to 475.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign narrative for 414-417; the Majorian page has Septimania Roman again in 458-460.

wars.name: Wars of Theodoric I at Arles, Narbonne and Toulouse
wars.outcome: Theodoric I attacked Arles, was beaten at Narbonne in 436 and, defeated the allied Romans and Huns at Toulouse in 439; no border moved after the 418 settlement.
wars.note: The page: 'Under Theodoric I (418-451), the Visigoths attacked Arles'; 'Theodoric's defeat at the Battle of Narbonne in 436'; 'in 439 at the Battle of Toulouse the Visigoths defeated the allied forces of Romans and Huns.' The page gives no year for the Arles attack; 425 is the first year of Theodoric's reign, since the page dates only 436 and 439.

wars.name: Vandal conquest of Africa
wars.outcome: The Vandals crossed in 429, besieged Hippo in 430, were settled in Numidia and Mauretania by the treaty of 435, took Carthage in 439 and gained Byzacena, Tripolitania and part of Numidia by the treaty of 442.
wars.note: Two treaties, 435 and 442, fix the frontier in words; the second also confirmed 'Proconsular Africa'.

wars.name: Aetius against the Burgundians
wars.outcome: Gundahar and many of the Burgundians were killed by Aetius, with Hun help, about 436; the survivors were resettled in Sapaudia in 443.
wars.note: 'In about 436'; the Huns were Aetius's allies.

wars.name: Frankish advance on Tournai and Cambrai
wars.outcome: The Franks took Tournai and Cambrai 'probably in the period 445-450'.
wars.note: The span is from Lanting and van der Plicht, cited on the page.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of Gaul

zones.text: Gaul between the Rhine and the Loire

wars.outcome: Attila crossed the Rhine in 451, took Metz on 7 April and reached Orléans; the Romans under Aetius, with the Visigoths under Theodoric, fought him at the Catalaunian Plains circa 20 June and he withdrew. No land was lost; recorded as an occupation (hatched), as in the huns dossier.
wars.note: The Visigothic page has Theodoric fighting 'under Flavius Aetius against Attila the Hun in the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains'; no month on either page.

wars.name: Hunnic invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Attila ravaged north-eastern Italy, razed Aquileia after a three-month siege, halted at the Po and withdrew; he died early in 453. Recorded as an occupation (hatched), as in the huns dossier.

wars.name: Vandal sack of Rome
wars.outcome: Gaiseric entered Rome; 'on 2 June 455, Pope Leo the Great received Gaiseric and implored him to abstain from murder'. No border moved.
wars.note: The Western Roman Empire page: 'The severity of the Vandal sack of 455 is disputed'.

wars.name: Majorian's reconquest of Gaul and Hispania

zones.text: Septimania and the Gaulish lands recovered
Hispania, the Suebi campaign of 459 and the fleet of 460

wars.outcome: Majorian entered Gaul in late 458, forced the Visigoths to federate status and give up Hispania, campaigned against the Suebi through 459 and gathered a fleet in 460 that the Vandals destroyed; he was murdered on 7 August 461 and the gains were not held.
wars.note: The Vandal page: 'Majorian ... began to organize an offensive in the summer of 458'; 'The Emperor assembled his fleet in 460, but Gaiseric learned of the impending assault'.

wars.name: Aegidius's refusal of Libius Severus
wars.outcome: Aegidius 'refused to recognize the new emperor Libius Severus (reigned 461-465), even threatening to invade Italy'; he held northern Gaul until his death in autumn 465, and his son Syagrius after him.
wars.note: No border is drawn; northern Gaul stays inside the shape until 476.

wars.name: Euric's conquests

zones.text: Baetica and the south of Hispania, 472
the lands south of the Loire and west of the Rhone, 475

wars.outcome: Euric took Mérida and most of Lusitania in 469, Arles after the Battle of Arles in 471, Tarraconensis (Visigothic page) and most of Hispania (Euric page) in 472, received the lands south of the Loire and west of the Rhone by the treaty of 475, which returned Provence, and had extended his rule to the Rhone and the Loire by 476.
wars.note: 'The Roman army was crushed at the nearby Battle of Arles (471), resulting in Euric capturing Arles' (Visigothic Kingdom); 'In 472 he conquered most of Hispania' (Euric).

wars.name: Odoacer's revolt against Orestes
wars.outcome: The foederati proclaimed Odoacer king on 23 August 476, Orestes was killed at Placentia, Romulus Augustulus abdicated on 4 September and Odoacer ruled Italy; Nepos kept Dalmatia until his murder in 480.

certainty.note: No survey lines; frontiers are provinces or river lines. The Vandal treaties of 435 and 442 and the 475 treaty with Euric name the provinces handed over and are the nearest to sharp; Cliopatria's Gaulish and Spanish edges from 455 are approximate.

notes:
Dates. Start 17 January 395 (division). End: the page's infobox ends the empire on 4 September 476 (Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus) and notes 9 May 480 (Nepos murdered) as an alternative; this dossier ends it in May 480 because the page has Nepos 'continue to reign as Western emperor from Dalmatia' and recognised by the East (Julius Nepos page), and because Cliopatria draws the Dalmatian cells in 476-479 (inside its Kingdom of Soissons row). Italy goes to Odoacer on 4 September 476; Dalmatia is Odoacer's from late 481 or 482, so 481 is a gap. Cliopatria rows. 18 shapes reviewed: ok 395, 396, 414, 417, 426, 455, 458, 462; adjust 402, 407, 410, 439, 441, 443, 459, 469; wrong 451, 452 (Attila's raids drawn as Hunnic land); new keyframes 408, 409, 429, 433, 435, 437, 469b, 471, 472, 476. Cliopatria's 469 shape drops Spain and the lands south of the Loire three to six years before the page (472 and 475); the 462 shape's Gaulish losses are early or unverified; Sapaudia is cut in 451, not 443; Carthage in 443, not 439. Counterparts that need dossiers: constantine-iii-usurper (rebel, 407-411, written in this batch), kingdom-of-odoacer (new state, 476-493, written in this batch); Gerontius's Maximus (slug maximus-usurper, not Magnus Maximus of 383-388; Hispania 409-411 and Gaul early to September 411), Jovinus (411-413) and the Bagaudae of Armorica (from 409) have no row and no dossier; Marcellinus (Dalmatia and Sicily) is unopened; the Alamanni, the Alans and the Suebi are Cliopatria rows of group eu-06. Overlaps and conflicts with the roman-empire dossier (eu-04-a): that dossier carries no matching loss for Spain in 261-269 and draws Spain throughout. Cliopatria's 'vandals' row (337-438) is used as the counterpart for losses before 439 ('visigoths' for 402-417): eu-06 may merge them with vandal-kingdom and visigothic-kingdom. Unverified in detail (page budget): the Alamannic advance (462), the Frankish extent beyond Belgica Secunda, Sardinia and Corsica (undated), Marcellinus and Sicily after 461, the 455-457 Gaulish cuts. Pages that would not give the fact: Attila (no Pannonia), Fall of the Western Roman Empire (thin), Western Roman Empire (no Aegidius, Euric, Burgundians, 442). Region names the gazetteer lacks: none unresolved at the last check beyond what --resolve reports. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review; pages reopened: Constantine III, Rugila, Euric, Visigothic Kingdom, Kingdom of the Suebi, Mauro-Roman Kingdom, Praetorian prefecture of Illyricum, Wallia, Battle of the Catalaunian Plains). (1) Hispania: Constans takes it early in 408 (Constantine III page), so the 407 shape is split (407 only; new 408 keyframe) and the 409 loss to the barbarians is withdrawn; the 414 gain now has Maximus's regime as counterpart at confidence 1. (2) Gaul 411: the September gain is Arles only (from Constantine III, as his dissolve); the rest of Gaul comes from Gerontius's Maximus (confidence 2). (3) Mirrors added: 429 Altava area to mauro-roman-kingdom, 433 Pannonia (Hungarian cells of the shape) to huns, 437 Sirmium (25 km) to eastern-roman-empire, each with a keyframe cut; the 435 Vandal loss leaves Altava out. (4) Spain 462-472: the 462 shape holds 1,743 Spanish cells (Lusitania 362, Baetica 403, Tarraconensis 1,061, none in Galicia); losses now dated 469 (Mérida to Euric, Lisbon to the Suebi), 472 (Baetica, Euric page; Tarraconensis, Visigothic page). (5) Arles: lost in 471 (Battle of Arles), regained in 475 ('in exchange for the return of Provence', Euric page), lost again in 476. (6) Attila's campaigns are occupation_start/end, as in huns /ledger/13-16, with months for 451 (7 April, circa 20 June). DISAGREEMENTS: the Euric page keeps the north-east with Barcelona Roman after 472 and has Nepos cede it in 475, the Visigothic page has Tarraconensis captured in 472 (472 kept, Euric page noted); the Euric page ties Berry to the Battle of Arles (471) while the Visigothic page has the lands south of the Loire granted in 475 (475 kept); the Rugila page dates the Pannonian cession 425, 431 or 433 (433 kept for the mirror with huns); {region: Pannonia} is used by the huns dossier but is not in the gazetteer, so Hungary (the only Pannonian cells of the shape) is used here; the Praetorian prefecture page gives Eastern sovereignty over the whole prefecture, but only Sirmium is moved, as eastern-roman-empire has it. Counterparts needing dossiers: maximus-usurper (Gerontius's Maximus, 409-411), jovinus (411-413); mirrors owed by others: kingdom-of-the-suebi (469 Lisbon), visigothic-kingdom (469, 471, 472, 475), mauro-roman-kingdom (429, present), huns (433, present), eastern-roman-empire (437, present). Not done, left to gap-fillers: the confidence-1 events listed by the reviewer (402 Britain strip, 407 Alaric, 417 Septimania, 439 Brabant, 441 Sicily, 442 return of the Mauretanias, 455 Ostrogoths and Visigoths, 458 Sardinia, 462 Sicily, Burgundians, Narbonne, Alamanni, Franks).
